title: Intent Phrase Lexicon
description: Locale-keyed phrase lists for heuristic intent classification. Each concept id is matched by libs/core/intent/intent-phrase-lexicon.ts (matchesIntentPhrase). Phrases are literal (escaped) strings; patterns are regex source strings for cases a literal cannot express (wildcards, optional suffixes, whitespace classes). Every locale is checked by default because the input language may differ from the UI locale; `und` holds language-neutral tokens such as product names.

prefix_word_suffixes.description: Per locale, short polite verb suffixes that may follow a prefix_word phrase ending in a non-ASCII character (停止 + して, 止めて + ください). Scripts without word spaces need these because \b cannot separate 停止 from 停止ボタン; a suffix only counts when it is itself followed by end of text, whitespace or punctuation. Longer suffixes should be listed before their prefixes.

flags.description: RegExp flags. Only case-insensitive (i) and unicode (u) are allowed; stateful flags (g, y) are rejected so compiled matchers stay reusable.

match.description: contains (default): match anywhere. exact: the whole text must be one alternative (^(?:...)$). prefix_word: text starts with an alternative. Phrases ending in an ASCII word char need an ASCII word boundary after them; phrases ending in a non-ASCII (e.g. Japanese) char must be followed by end of text, whitespace, punctuation (、。！!？?), an ASCII word char, or a short polite suffix from prefix_word_suffixes (して / ください / …) that is itself followed by a clause end — never by a noun or particle (停止ボタン / キャンセルを).

word_boundary.description: ascii: literal phrases whose first/last character is an ASCII word character match as whole words (e.g. 'me' does not match inside 'meeting'). Non-ASCII phrases are unaffected.

patterns.description: Regex source strings (max 200 chars each). ReDoS guard limits: (1) the matcher rejects nested quantifiers such as (a+)+, (?:.*x)* or (a|b*){2,} at compile time; (2) it does NOT detect other super-linear shapes, e.g. a lazy capture between delimiters followed by .* ("(.+?)".*x is cubic on a run of quotes) or overlapping adjacent quantifiers (\s*\s*). Prefer negated classes for delimited captures ("([^"]+)", 「([^」]+)」). libs/core/intent/intent-phrase-lexicon.test.ts runs every concept against adversarial 5,000-char inputs under a time budget; a new pattern that trips it must be rewritten, not the budget raised.
